messages:
sara.j: 🚨 Alert from sec-alert-bot: sudden spike in service-account token creation + key-rotate events across us-west1 and eu-central1. Pattern looks like a credential 'waterfall' — many short-lived tokens issued then used from multiple IPs. Seen in audit-auth and kms-access logs.
ops-bot: [ALERT] credential_waterfall_detected severity=high affected_services=[auth,k8s-api,kms] first_seen=2064320902 count=124
jess.c: copying logs to #incidents, grabbing full auth audit slices now. Is this tied to any recent RBAC rollout?
sara.j: not that I can see in the deploy logs. last RBAC change was 2064316000 (read-only role tweak). This looks like programmatic key creation.
alex.t: I'll run a quick query. gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.iam.admin.v1.CreateServiceAccountKey\" AND timestamp>\"2026-11-02T02:30:00Z\"" --limit 50 --format json > /tmp/key-creations.json
mike.k: good call. Also check user_agent + ip: could be a compromised CI runner or an API key leak.
natalie.p: I see repeated calls from service-account: infra-ci-sa@redwood-prod.ips in the logs, originating from 18.45.12.0/24 and 3.5.6.0/24.
sara.j: immediate containment plan: 1) revoke keys for infra-ci-sa (temporary) 2) rotate KMS wrapping keys for affected envelopes 3) block offending CIDRs at firewall 4) enable audit-log streaming to S3 bucket for forensic copy. Agree?
jess.c: +1. I'll revoke keys and add a deny binding for the service account in IAM. Command: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=infra-ci-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format="value(name)" | xargs -I {} gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete {} --iam-account=infra-ci-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -q
```
sara.j: after key revocation, push temporary policy to prevent token creation from that SA: add role iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator denial at org level for that principal.
ops-bot: [ACTION] runbook-step executed=key_revocation actor=jess.c ts=2064321120
mike.k: blocking CIDRs at edge now. fw rule create --direction=INGRESS --action=DENY --source-ranges=18.45.12.0/24,3.5.6.0/24 --target-tags=external-api - applied 2064321165
alex.t: starting KMS rewrap for affected secrets. I'll snapshot list via: 
```
gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=redwood-secrets --format=json > /tmp/kms-keys.json
```
natalie.p: collecting evidence: I'm pulling CloudTrail/audit logs, k8s audit, and kubelet logs for nodes that saw traffic. Packaging to forensic bucket redwood-forensics/2064321007/.
sara.j: decision: no public PII exfil confirmed yet. Treat as active compromise. Notify trust & safety and legal. @natalie.p please escalate.
jess.c: legal and trust notified at 2064321210.
mike.k: preliminary impact: CI pipelines using infra-ci-sa are now failing — rolling-back policy to unblock dev will create risk, so keep services frozen until we verify.
sara.j: timeline note: detected 2064320902, containment started 2064321120 (key revocation), CIDR block 2064321165, KMS rewrap start 2064321220. Add these to incident timeline.
ops-bot: [NOTE] evidence_bundle_location=gs://redwood-forensics/2064321007/ files=auth_logs.json,kms_access.json,k8s_audit.json
alex.t: Found a pattern: new keys created, then used to call GenerateAccessToken for downstream GCP services — suggests lateral session propagation. Might be a leaked service token fed into CI runners.
natalie.p: collecting runner metadata from buildkite and self-hosted runners now — correlating build IDs with IPs.
sara.j: assign roles: incident lead = sara.j, containment = jess.c, forensics = natalie.p, comms = mike.k.
jess.c: starting forensic copy of keys database and storing checksums.
mike.k: drafting incident banner for internal status page: "Active security incident: credential compromise affecting infra-ci service account; containment in progress. Do not rotate or re-enable infra-ci-sa until notified."
ops-bot: [PAGE] oncall-next=night@mike.k handoff_window_start=2064321400
sara.j: handoff plan: we'll stabilize for 30m, then hand to night oncall with full timeline and action items. mike, you'll take the night handoff if stable?
mike.k: I can take it. I'll validate KMS rewrap completes and that no new key creations appear in the logs for 15m before accepting.
sara.j: agreed. Final actions for handoff: 1) confirm no new key creates in last 15m 2) ensure firewall blocks persist 3) upload full evidence bundle link in the incident tracker 4) list of revoked keys and rotated KMS keys.
natalie.p: uploading evidence bundle now (2064321290). link: gs://redwood-forensics/2064321007/complete_bundle.zip
sara.j: OK locking incident channel. Thanks all. Handoff to @mike.k at 2064321400. If anything spikes, ping pager. :lock:
